Guarantees that items and crates within claimed faction/player safehouses are strictly protected.
Number of tiles scanned per engine frame during background sweeps.
Deletes distant animal track footprint entities outside tracking radius to save CPU and savefile size.
Maximum allowed active animal audio emitters in an area.
Caps simultaneous animal sound emitters in crowded livestock pens.
Automatically protects TrueMusic, custom gun sound packs, and voice mods from audio throttling.
Shields player-built bases, water collector barrels, fuel cans, and generators from all sweeps.
Periodically removes accumulated ground blood decals around the player based on your configured interval.
Caps overlapping blood splats to max 4 per single tile. Eliminates severe GPU overdraw lag during large battles while keeping the scene 100%% bloody.
Tile radius around the player checked during blood sweeps.
In-game hours between automatic blood decal cleanup sweeps.
Also scrubs blood splatters from walls, windows, and furniture during blood sweeps.
Performs an immediate all-in-one maintenance sweep (Blood + Corpses + Ground Debris + RAM Purge) in your local area.
Manually removes floor and wall blood decals within your configured radius.
Manually purges empty or junk zombie corpses in radius while strictly preserving weapons, bags, ammo, and keys.
Manually clears spent bullet casings, empty tins, broken glass, and twigs from the ground.
Periodically sweeps away aged zombie corpses in your local zone to reduce CPU entity tracking.
Immediately sweeps away skeletonized dead bodies and burnt ash piles to keep streets clean.
Only removes corpses whose inventory is completely empty, ensuring 100%% of zombie loot is preserved.
Cleans corpses that only carry worn clothes while strictly saving weapons, ammo, bags, keys, and watches.
Tile radius around the player checked during corpse sweeps.
Disables dynamic 3D shadow stencils on dead corpses to save draw calls in horde battles.
In-game hours between automated zombie corpse sweeps.
Minimum hours a corpse must have been dead before it is eligible for cleanup.
Silences annoying buzzing fly audio emitters on dead zombie bodies.
Periodically scans and cleans clutter items dropped in the world based on the item filters below.
Cleans dangerous broken window glass shards on the floor to prevent tire punctures and lacerations.
Cleans up spent bullet shells and empty ammunition casings on the floor (supports vanilla and gun mods).
Distance in tiles around the player to search for ground debris.
Purges completely rotten expired food items left dropped on the ground to reduce save bloat.
Removes discarded empty food cans, empty soda bottles, candy wrappers, and cigarette butts.
Removes naturally spawned foraging twigs, tree branches, and stones from roadways and paved areas (Logs and log stacks are permanently protected).
In-game hours between ground clutter and trash cleanup sweeps.
Optimizes cutaway wall and multi-story occlusion calculations for smooth interior frame rates.
Caps overlapping burning zombie scream sound loops.
Caps maximum active fire particles to 50 and vortices to 2 during large building and zombie fires.
Memory usage cutoff threshold required before Smart Idle Garbage Collection triggers a background sweep.
Runs gentle memory sweeps only when you are safely sleeping, reading, or resting indoors with zero nearby zombies.
Culls hidden lower floors and unviewable exterior ground tiles when inside multi-story buildings and skyscrapers. Automatically restores near windows & balconies.

Enables the mod's optimized screen-space puddle wave shaders and multi-pass wall shaders. Uncheck to bypass all custom shaders and use high-speed 2D flat tiles/puddles (recommended for Potato mode or if experiencing GPU driver glitches).
Disabling eliminates secondary reflection passes on roads and puddles, curing Build 42 driving and rain stutter.
Dynamically scales sub-pixel ground debris and skeleton blending when zoomed out to 150-250%% to eliminate zoom-out frame lag.
Forces texture compression in options.ini, cutting VRAM usage in half and stopping texture loading hitching.
Uncheck in Potato Mode to shade character/zombie meshes with ambient room light rather than per-vertex dynamic point lights.
Transitions distant zombies into stepped LOD animation poses sooner, eliminating frame drops when large swarms approach.
Limits simultaneous overlapping zombie groan and footstep audio emitters to the nearest 16 zombies to stop audio crackling and FMOD CPU lag.
[EXPERIMENTAL] Renders distant zombies in large 100+ hordes as 2D billboard imposters & enables GPU mesh instancing. WARNING: May cause micro-stutters during combat state transitions.
Skips skeletal mesh bone and animation math for zombies outside your camera view.
Staggers zombie A* navigation recalculations across a 4-phase round-robin cycle to drop swarm AI CPU load by 75%%.
Reduces skeletal animation update frequency for idle, sleeping, or standing characters to 15 FPS to save massive CPU cycles.
Hotkey used to toggle the Project Zomboid Optimiser Control Center (Default: F10)
Compiles character clothing, armor, and vehicle 3D textures across background CPU threads to eliminate equipment swap frame drops.
Directly patches IsoGridSquare.splatBlood in JVM bytecode to instantly return if a tile already has blood. Completely eliminates chunk FBO texture rebinding stalls in high-kill combats.
Keeps recently streamed road and town chunks cached in 8GB+ RAM to completely eliminate disk read stutters when turning around or retracing paths.
Bypasses heavy wall-occlusion and low-pass DSP calculations for sounds beyond 35 tiles or below hearing threshold. Lowers audio thread CPU load during 100+ zombie combat.
Dynamically adjusts FSR render scale based on real-time frametime headroom against target FPS (down to 65% or chosen scale) to absorb sudden horde or weather spikes.
Renders the 3D world at performance scale and reconstructs it with AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution (EASU + RCAS) while UI text stays native. Massive FPS boost on 1440p, 4K, and handhelds.
Upscaling render resolution preset. Ultra Quality (77%) provides near-native image clarity with 30-50%+ FPS gains; Performance (50%) provides maximum boost.
Robust Contrast-Adaptive Sharpening strength (0% = soft, 80% = recommended, 100% = max crispness).
Filters redundant shader uniform uploads (lighting, fog, ambient color) and 3D clothing bone matrices before sending them to the GPU driver. Boosts FPS in dense cities.
Hibernates distant off-screen zombie pathfinding and animation state in RAM buffers to save massive CPU cycles in mega-horde territory.
Smoothly collects Lua garbage in 50-step increments every frame to prevent dead mod tables from accumulating and triggering 20-30ms stutter spikes during vehicle travel.
Locks Windows/Linux multimedia high-performance thread scheduling and prioritizes Performance Cores (P-Cores) over Efficiency Cores on Intel 12th-15th Gen and AMD X3D CPUs.
Immediately triggers a native JVM and Kahlua memory collection cycle to release unreferenced heap memory.
Enables 128KB page-aligned direct NIO memory stream buffers and ChunkBufferPool for stutter-free road chunk loading at 70+ mph.
Eliminates in-game stop-the-world Lua garbage collection pauses during combat and driving by offloading memory management to background G1GC worker threads.
Controls the target update framerate for dynamic lighting propagation. Lower values (15-30 FPS) save huge CPU cycles.

Comprehensive protection suite against 3rd-party mods: neutralizes forced GC freezes during combat/driving, throttles disk I/O log spam (100%% preserves errors), and shields Build 42 vehicle mechanics from malformed recipe crashes.
Throttles expensive 60 Hz per-frame pipe flow loops in Water Pipes and irrigation mods down to 1 Hz, dropping CPU load by 98%% with zero gameplay loss.
Recommended for modern systems. Stutter-free combat, safe blood cap (4/tile), texture compression, and safehouse protection with zero visual loss.
EXPERIMENTAL: Enables 2D billboard imposters, GPU mesh instancing, and threaded lighting. WARNING: May cause micro-stutters during combat state transitions.
Minimalist mode: Enables audio channel limits and memory management without automated world entity purges.
Aggressive stutter-free boost for low-end hardware. Caps blood to 1/tile, culls corpse shadows, clamps rain particles, 15 FPS lighting refresh, and automated cleanup sweeps.
Optimized profile for multiplayer dedicated servers. Automates scheduled sweeps, protects safehouses, and purges world clutter.
BENCHMARK MODE: Disables 100%% of all mod features so you can measure raw baseline performance as if the mod was never installed.
Instantly forces a dual-pass garbage collection cycle to reclaim orphaned Lua tables, closures, and dead userdata.
Scans the active Lua VM to measure memory tables and active event hooks for all mods.
Encountering an issue or crash? Click to package your console.txt and pzo_engine.log diagnostics for GitHub.
Resets all configuration values to factory balanced defaults.
Saves your configuration to disk and closes the Optimiser Control Center.
Transfers and saves your current Optimiser settings directly into the dedicated server configuration file on disk, without needing to manually edit or upload server files.
Instant one-click manual cleanup tools and live real-time performance diagnostics.

Optional hardware-level JVM optimizations: zero-stutter background GC, deep RAM chunk caching, async 3D model compiling, and horde hibernation.
Anti-stutter vehicle road streaming, parked car physics sleeper, auto-zoom limiter, and roadside entity throttles.

Accelerates inventory rendering and eliminates scrolling stutters in containers with 500+ items via tooltip throttling and bulk transfer debounce.

Prioritizes road chunk loading bandwidth and throttles non-essential systems while driving.

Scales dynamic lighting update rate during high-speed travel. Recommended: OFF so newly streamed road chunks are lit promptly without lighting lag.
Driving speed in km/h required to trigger high-speed chunk streaming prioritization.
Temporarily pauses tile sweeps, corpse checks, and RAM purges while driving for smooth road loading.
Offloads 3D vehicle parts and clothing loading to background threads instead of freezing the render loop.

Caps the frame rate at what this PC holds steadily, measured from a performance recording, so the game stops swinging between fast and slow moments. It picks a rate that divides your screen's refresh rate when it can, and never goes above the game's own limit. Laptops run cooler and slow down less when hot. It can't fix freezes from loading the map, saving or mods; the recording's report says where those come from. Lifted while a new recording runs, and every new recording measures again.
Caps fire particles, fire objects and smoke in large fires, and burning characters no longer light their surroundings.
Runs a full memory sweep only while you sleep, read or rest, and only above the threshold below.
Inside a multi-story building, floors you cannot see are not drawn. Restored outside and in vehicles.
The game's wall, puddle and water shaders (on in vanilla). Turning them off saves GPU time but looks flatter. Turn off if you see shader glitches on your GPU.
The game's reflection pass on roads and puddles. Looks better, costs GPU, most of all in rain.
When zoomed out to 150 percent or more, fewer zombies get fully blended animations. Your normal setting comes back when you zoom in.
Turns on the game's texture compression in options.ini. Textures use far less video memory and load with fewer hitches.
Trees and bushes far from you are drawn into the chunk's cached image instead of being redrawn every frame with wind sway. Stands down when Atmospherics is active.
Lights characters and zombies with nearby light sources (on in vanilla). Off uses the room's ambient light instead.
Distant zombies switch to cheaper, stepped animation sooner.
Fewer zombies groan at once: only the nearest ones, as set below, get a voice (the game allows 20).
Items worn on belts, backs and holsters of zombies more than 25 tiles from you are not drawn. Their items are untouched and reappear as they come closer.
Distant zombies in large hordes are drawn as flat 2D images, with instanced rendering. May stutter when zombies change state.
Uses the game's animation delay for zombies outside your view, so their skeletons update less often.
Characters standing still, sleeping or idle update their animation 15 times a second instead of 30.
Clothing and vehicle textures larger than your texture size option are shrunk on a worker thread instead of in the frame, removing a 100 to 250 ms hitch per large texture.
A tile that already has blood gets no more, which avoids re-drawing its chunk image on every hit.
Lowers the render scale (down to 65 percent) when a frame runs over your target frame time, and raises it again when there is headroom.
Renders the world below your resolution and upscales it with FSR 1.0. The UI stays sharp.
Shader values and bone matrices identical to what the GPU already has are not sent again.
Zombies no player can see update less often when your frame rate is high, as the game already does at lower frame rates.
Answers queued path requests until the time below is used up, instead of the game's fixed 2 per pass, so zombies start moving sooner.
A faster priority queue inside the game's pathfinding library, so paths are found sooner in hordes and complex buildings.
Several changes to the same square in one pass are sent to the pathfinder as one.
A moving vehicle's shape is re-sent to the pathfinder only after it moves a quarter tile or every 250 ms.
Sets the 0.5 ms system timer, exempts the game from Windows power throttling, and on CPUs with enough cores uses MMCSS game scheduling and a higher process priority.
When the Java heap is about to need a collection, it is started in a frame that has time to spare, instead of landing mid-step during combat or driving.
How many times a second dynamic lighting is recalculated. Presets set this too.
Mods that force a full memory sweep mid-game are held back until you sleep, read or rest. Each repeated mod error is printed only 3 times. Broken vehicle repair recipes from mods are repaired.

Other mods' per-frame scripts run 60 times a second on average, spread over frames. At 60 FPS or less nothing changes, and they always run on a frame with a key or mouse press. Real Limbs and Project A-Life are left alone.

Other mods' scripts that run on every map square as it loads (LoadGridsquare) are queued and run over the next frames, about 2 ms per frame, squares nearest you first. With many mods this is most of the stutter while driving. A mod's change to a new square can show up a moment later. A mod that needs it straight away can be listed below.
Other mods' per-zombie scripts run every frame within 15 tiles of you, every 3rd frame to 30 tiles and every 6th beyond. Real Limbs and Project A-Life are left alone.
Runs the per-frame updates of Water Pipes and irrigation mods once a second. Only matters with those mods.
Moves dynamic lighting updates to a background thread. May cause short stalls in heavy combat.
Skips rebuilding the inventory item tooltip while the mouse is not moving.

Fallen twigs, branches and loose stones. Logs are never removed.
Uses the game's cheaper occlusion count for cutaway walls and upper floors.

Caps the frame rate at what this PC holds steadily, measured from a performance recording, so the game stops swinging between fast and slow moments. It picks a rate that divides your screen's refresh rate when it can, and never goes above the game's own limit. Laptops run cooler and slow down less when hot. It can't fix freezes from loading the map, saving or mods; the recording's report says where those come from. Lifted while a new recording runs, and every new recording measures again.
Caps fire particles, fire objects and smoke in large fires, and burning characters no longer light their surroundings.
Runs a full memory sweep only while you sleep, read or rest, and only above the threshold below.
Inside a multi-story building, floors you cannot see are not drawn. Restored outside and in vehicles.
The game's wall, puddle and water shaders (on in vanilla). Turning them off saves GPU time but looks flatter. Turn off if you see shader glitches on your GPU.
The game's reflection pass on roads and puddles. Looks better, costs GPU, most of all in rain.
When zoomed out to 150 percent or more, fewer zombies get fully blended animations. Your normal setting comes back when you zoom in.
Turns on the game's texture compression in options.ini. Textures use far less video memory and load with fewer hitches.
Bushes, grass and fences far from you are drawn into the chunk's cached image instead of being redrawn every frame with wind sway. Stands down when Atmospherics is active.
Lights characters and zombies with nearby light sources (on in vanilla). Off uses the room's ambient light instead.
Distant zombies switch to cheaper, stepped animation sooner.
Fewer zombies groan at once: only the nearest ones, as set below, get a voice (the game allows 20).
Items worn on belts, backs and holsters of zombies more than 25 tiles from you are not drawn. Their items are untouched and reappear as they come closer.
Distant zombies in large hordes are drawn as flat 2D images, with instanced rendering. May stutter when zombies change state.
Uses the game's animation delay for zombies outside your view, so their skeletons update less often.
Characters standing still, sleeping or idle update their animation 15 times a second instead of 30.

At every launch the game reads and converts more than 2,200 animation files (about 500 MB of text), which takes several seconds of loading. The converted animations are now kept in Zomboid/PZO/animcache.bin (about 85 MB) and reused while the files are unchanged, about 17 times faster per file. One cached animation in 64 is also converted the normal way and compared, and any difference turns the cache off. It is rebuilt by itself after a game update.
Clothing and vehicle textures larger than your texture size option are shrunk on a worker thread instead of in the frame, removing a 100 to 250 ms hitch per large texture.
A tile that already has blood gets no more, which avoids re-drawing its chunk image on every hit.

How many chunks around you are kept loaded and simulated. Auto is the game's own size for your screen (19 by 19 chunks at 1080p and above). Smaller saves CPU and memory while travelling and near hordes; zombies outside the loaded area stay inactive until you come closer.

The game draws each chunk into a cached image and threw that image away the moment the chunk left the screen, so it had to be drawn again from scratch as soon as it came back, often in frames already busy loading the world. Images are now kept for a while off screen (a small share of video memory, at most 256 MB; not used on integrated graphics or cards with 4 GB or less) and reused if nothing in the chunk changed. Same picture.

Every frame the game worked out again which buildings in front of you and the squares around you should be cut away, walking the same squares into a new list each time. That answer is now reused while you and the squares around you haven't moved, and worked out again at least every 8 frames. Same cut-aways.

Java 25, which Build 42 runs on, can store every object with a smaller header. The game keeps millions of small objects (map squares, sprites, Lua tables), so it uses less memory and the CPU caches hold more of what it is working on. Only used when the game's Java is version 25 or newer.

For older or low-end PCs: the game no longer reserves and touches its whole starting memory before it starts, starts with a small heap that grows as needed, uses the G1 collector, and PZO leaves the process priority and memory locking alone. Auto turns it on for a CPU without AVX2, 4 or fewer threads, or less than 7.5 GB of RAM.

When zombies in a crowd push each other apart, the wall, door and window check between two squares is worked out once per frame instead of once per zombie. Any door or wall change clears it at once. Same movement.

Near or inside a building, every step re-drew the cached image of each chunk holding a cut-away wall, even when the same walls stayed cut. Now only chunks where a wall was actually cut or restored are re-drawn. Same picture.

To work out which walls to cut away, the game walked every wall on your floor of every chunk on screen once for each visible square around you, though the first walk already finds everything. It now walks them once, and skips walls that can't be cut away at all. Same cut-aways.

The game loads a depth map for every tile set (it decides what is drawn in front of what). Its loader threads took turns, so the maps loaded one file at a time. They now load side by side, so the loading screen finishes sooner. The maps are identical.
Lowers the render scale (down to 65 percent) when a frame runs over your target frame time, and raises it again when there is headroom.
Renders the world below your resolution and upscales it with FSR 1.0. The UI stays sharp.
Zombies more than 20 tiles from you look for a door, window or fence ahead of them every other frame instead of every frame. They reach it at most one frame later. Zombies near you are unchanged.

The game strips comments from its script and map files in a way that slows down badly on big files: the 6.5 MB tile geometry file alone took seconds on every launch. Comments are now removed in one pass, and duplicate vehicle zones and zombie density lookups are handled without rescanning while a save loads. The result is identical.

When a new row of chunks comes into view, the game draws all of their cached images in the same frame, which makes up much of the stutter while driving. Now at most 8 start per frame; distant chunks wait up to 3 frames, so one may appear a moment late at the screen edge. Chunks near you are never delayed.

In fog, the game walked every square on screen each frame only to step through the fog rows, which it then steps through again at the end anyway. The fog is now built in that last step alone. Same fog.
Shader values and bone matrices identical to what the GPU already has are not sent again.
Zombies no player can see update less often when your frame rate is high, as the game already does at lower frame rates.

On PCs with two graphics chips, which includes most gaming laptops, Windows often runs the game on the slower power-saving one built into the CPU. This sets the game to High performance in Windows' own graphics settings (Settings > Display > Graphics), so it runs on the dedicated GPU. A choice you already made there is kept, and turning this off removes the setting again. Does nothing on PCs with one graphics card.

Before drawing, the game asks the lighting engine about each square on screen, and a square whose light hadn't changed was asked again on every lookup, several times a frame. It's now asked once per lighting update. Same light.

Every launch and every save load the game compiles each Lua file it runs, its own and every mod's, from scratch. Compiled files are now kept in Zomboid/PZO/luacache.bin and reused while the file is unchanged, so starting the game and loading saves is quicker. The cache is rebuilt by itself after a game update.

Lua functions that run a lot (other mods', the game's and this one's) are turned into Java code after a few thousand instructions, so Java compiles them to machine code. In tests mod-style Lua ran 2 to 4 times faster. Function calls, errors and coroutines still go through the game's own Lua, so mods behave the same. A mod that misbehaves can be excluded below.

While new models load, the game raised an internal error for every bone it does not know (props, vehicle parts, modded rigs), and a model whose texture name the file system rejects failed and was logged again every time it loaded. Bones are now looked up in a table, and a bad texture name fails once and is logged once. Same result, fewer hitches while the world streams in.

Noises zombies can hear are listed in every chunk they reach. Those lists are now cleaned only in a frame where a noise actually ran out, instead of checking every loaded chunk every frame. Same noises.

The map of squares hidden behind upper floors was rebuilt almost every frame, because lights change a little all the time. It is now rebuilt only when walls, floors, cut-aways, the view or the zoom changed. Same picture. Single player only.
Answers queued path requests until the time below is used up, instead of the game's fixed 2 per pass, so zombies start moving sooner.
A faster priority queue inside the game's pathfinding library, so paths are found sooner in hordes and complex buildings.
Several changes to the same square in one pass are sent to the pathfinder as one.
A moving vehicle's shape is re-sent to the pathfinder only after it moves a quarter tile or every 250 ms.

Every few hundred sprites the game re-created, mapped and unmapped its sprite buffers, six driver calls each time and many times a frame at a wide zoom. With OpenGL 4.4 they now stay mapped and are written directly, so the CPU hands sprites to the graphics card with far less driver work. Same picture. Older graphics drivers keep the normal path.
Sets the 0.5 ms system timer, exempts the game from Windows power throttling, and on CPUs with enough cores uses MMCSS game scheduling and a higher process priority.

At medium and high puddle quality, every frame re-checked each puddle square on screen and worked out its corner lights and depths again. Squares, lights and depths are now kept per chunk and refreshed only when that chunk is redrawn, its lights change or the camera moves. Same picture.

At the lowest puddle quality, puddles are painted into each chunk's cached image, and while rain fills or dries them the game re-drew every loaded chunk, roofs and basements included, about once a second. Now only chunk floors that actually have puddles are re-drawn. Same picture.
Those once-a-second puddle re-draws are spread over about a quarter of a second instead of all landing in one frame. Until its turn, a chunk shows its puddles one tiny step (1/500) behind the rain.

While a world loads, the game checks the ID of every building and room on the map about six times. It only writes errors to the log and fixes nothing. The check is skipped unless the game runs in debug mode, so big and modded maps load faster.

A zombie that is not making any sound no longer recalculates its sound settings (floor material, distance, inside or out) every frame. They are worked out fresh the moment it makes a sound. Same sounds.

While the game starts and a save loads, finished textures wait in a queue for the graphics card. The game keeps that queue small and only sends it between loading-screen frames, so the loader threads often sit idle. The queue may now hold more (128 MB with 8 GB of RAM, 256 MB with 16 GB) and is sent as soon as work arrives. Nothing changes once you are playing.
The game profiler and the tile depth helper look up a per-thread value thousands of times a frame. On the game thread that value never changes, so it is now handed back straight away.

Chain-link fences, scaffolding, street decorations and ornamental plants near you are drawn into the chunk's cached image too, instead of one by one every frame. On a bench they were 91%% of what was still drawn every frame. They don't sway, so the picture is the same; ones the cache can't draw faithfully stay as they were.

Trees far from you are drawn into the chunk's cached image instead of one by one every frame, so they stop swaying in the wind. Trees near you, and large trees ahead of you while driving, are drawn as before.

Every update the game checked every crafting station, container and other object in the world to see if the player using it had walked away. Now only the objects someone is actually using are checked. Same result.
When the Java heap is about to need a collection, it is started in a frame that has time to spare, instead of landing mid-step during combat or driving.

When an area next to a horde loads, its zombies are created over a few frames instead of all in one long frame. Zombies within 25 tiles of you, and every zombie while you drive, still appear at once; none waits longer than half a second, and all are created before the game saves.

The distance zombies walk, crawl and run is added to the game's statistics once per frame instead of once per zombie, which also checks the achievements once instead of thousands of times. Same totals.
How many times a second dynamic lighting is recalculated. Auto leaves the game's own setting alone. Presets set this too.
Mods that force a full memory sweep mid-game are held back until you sleep, read or rest. Each repeated mod error is printed only 3 times. Broken vehicle repair recipes from mods are repaired.

Other mods' per-frame scripts run 60 times a second on average, spread over frames. At 60 FPS or less nothing changes, and they always run on a frame with a key or mouse press. Real Limbs and Project A-Life are left alone.

Other mods' scripts that run on every map square as it loads (LoadGridsquare) are queued and run over the next frames, about 2 ms per frame, squares nearest you first. With many mods this is most of the stutter while driving. A mod's change to a new square can show up a moment later. A mod that needs it straight away can be listed below.
Other mods' per-zombie scripts run every frame within 15 tiles of you, every 3rd frame to 30 tiles and every 6th beyond. Real Limbs and Project A-Life are left alone.
Runs the per-frame updates of Water Pipes and irrigation mods once a second. Only matters with those mods.
Moves dynamic lighting updates to a background thread. May cause short stalls in heavy combat.

Vehicle parts and clothing models are prepared on background threads instead of stalling the frame.

Nothing inside a claimed safehouse is touched by any cleanup.
How many tiles background cleanups check per frame.
Removes aged animal footprints far from you.
Master switch for the animal option below.
Animals more than 35 tiles away stop making sounds once the number below are already heard nearby.
Player-built structures, barrels, fuel cans and generators are never touched by any cleanup.
Removes floor blood around you on a timer.
Limits how many blood splats pile up on one tile.
Blood cleanup also removes splatter on walls, not just floors.
Blood and corpse changes from many kills at once re-draw many cached chunk images in one frame. They are spread over a few frames instead; the old image shows meanwhile.
Removes old zombie corpses around you on a timer, outside safehouses and player bases.
Only removes corpses with nothing left on them.
Also removes corpses carrying only junk; any corpse with weapons, bags, ammo or keys is kept.
Turns off the game's corpse shadows.
Removes the kinds of ground clutter chosen below around you on a timer. Logs, player bases and safehouses are never touched.
Glass shards on the ground.
Bullet casings and shotgun shells.
Fully rotten food lying on the ground.
Empty cans, bottles, wrappers, ashes and cigarette butts.
Fallen twigs, branches and loose stones. Logs are never removed.
Uses the game's cheaper occlusion count for cutaway walls and upper floors.

Caps the frame rate at what this PC holds steadily, measured from a performance recording, so the game stops swinging between fast and slow moments. It picks a rate that divides your screen's refresh rate when it can, and never goes above the game's own limit. Laptops run cooler and slow down less when hot. It can't fix freezes from loading the map, saving or mods; the recording's report says where those come from. Lifted while a new recording runs, and every new recording measures again.
Caps fire particles, fire objects and smoke in large fires, and burning characters no longer light their surroundings.
Runs a full memory sweep only while you sleep, read or rest, and only above the threshold below.
Inside a multi-story building, floors you cannot see are not drawn. Restored outside and in vehicles.
The game's wall, puddle and water shaders (on in vanilla). Turning them off saves GPU time but looks flatter. Turn off if you see shader glitches on your GPU.
The game's reflection pass on roads and puddles. Looks better, costs GPU, most of all in rain.
When zoomed out to 150 percent or more, fewer zombies get fully blended animations. Your normal setting comes back when you zoom in.
Turns on the game's texture compression in options.ini. Textures use far less video memory and load with fewer hitches.
Bushes, grass and fences far from you are drawn into the chunk's cached image instead of being redrawn every frame with wind sway. Stands down when Atmospherics is active.
Lights characters and zombies with nearby light sources (on in vanilla). Off uses the room's ambient light instead.
Distant zombies switch to cheaper, stepped animation sooner.
Fewer zombies groan at once: only the nearest ones, as set below, get a voice (the game allows 20).
Items worn on belts, backs and holsters of zombies more than 25 tiles from you are not drawn. Their items are untouched and reappear as they come closer.
Distant zombies in large hordes are drawn as flat 2D images, with instanced rendering. May stutter when zombies change state.
Uses the game's animation delay for zombies outside your view, so their skeletons update less often.
Characters standing still, sleeping or idle update their animation 15 times a second instead of 30.

At every launch the game reads and converts more than 2,200 animation files (about 500 MB of text), which takes several seconds of loading. The converted animations are now kept in Zomboid/PZO/animcache.bin (about 85 MB) and reused while the files are unchanged, about 17 times faster per file. One cached animation in 64 is also converted the normal way and compared, and any difference turns the cache off. It is rebuilt by itself after a game update.
Clothing and vehicle textures larger than your texture size option are shrunk on a worker thread instead of in the frame, removing a 100 to 250 ms hitch per large texture.
A tile that already has blood gets no more, which avoids re-drawing its chunk image on every hit.

How many chunks around you are kept loaded and simulated. Auto is the game's own size for your screen (19 by 19 chunks at 1080p and above). Smaller saves CPU and memory while travelling and near hordes; zombies outside the loaded area stay inactive until you come closer.

The game draws each chunk into a cached image and threw that image away the moment the chunk left the screen, so it had to be drawn again from scratch as soon as it came back, often in frames already busy loading the world. Images are now kept for a while off screen (a small share of video memory, at most 256 MB; not used on integrated graphics or cards with 4 GB or less) and reused if nothing in the chunk changed. Same picture.

Every frame the game worked out again which buildings in front of you and the squares around you should be cut away, walking the same squares into a new list each time. That answer is now reused while you and the squares around you haven't moved, and worked out again at least every 8 frames. Same cut-aways.

Java 25, which Build 42 runs on, can store every object with a smaller header. The game keeps millions of small objects (map squares, sprites, Lua tables), so it uses less memory and the CPU caches hold more of what it is working on. Only used when the game's Java is version 25 or newer.

For older or low-end PCs: the game no longer reserves and touches its whole starting memory before it starts, starts with a small heap that grows as needed, uses the G1 collector, and PZO leaves the process priority and memory locking alone. Auto turns it on for a CPU without AVX2, 4 or fewer threads, or less than 7.5 GB of RAM.

When zombies in a crowd push each other apart, the wall, door and window check between two squares is worked out once per frame instead of once per zombie. Any door or wall change clears it at once. Same movement.

Near or inside a building, every step re-drew the cached image of each chunk holding a cut-away wall, even when the same walls stayed cut. Now only chunks where a wall was actually cut or restored are re-drawn. Same picture.

To work out which walls to cut away, the game walked every wall on your floor of every chunk on screen once for each visible square around you, though the first walk already finds everything. It now walks them once, and skips walls that can't be cut away at all. Same cut-aways.

The game loads a depth map for every tile set (it decides what is drawn in front of what). Its loader threads took turns, so the maps loaded one file at a time. They now load side by side, so the loading screen finishes sooner. The maps are identical.
Lowers the render scale (down to 65 percent) when a frame runs over your target frame time, and raises it again when there is headroom.
Renders the world below your resolution and upscales it with FSR 1.0. The UI stays sharp.
Zombies more than 20 tiles from you look for a door, window or fence ahead of them every other frame instead of every frame. They reach it at most one frame later. Zombies near you are unchanged.

The game strips comments from its script and map files in a way that slows down badly on big files: the 6.5 MB tile geometry file alone took seconds on every launch. Comments are now removed in one pass, and duplicate vehicle zones and zombie density lookups are handled without rescanning while a save loads. The result is identical.

When a new row of chunks comes into view, the game draws all of their cached images in the same frame, which makes up much of the stutter while driving. Now at most 8 start per frame; distant chunks wait up to 3 frames, so one may appear a moment late at the screen edge. Chunks near you are never delayed.

In fog, the game walked every square on screen each frame only to step through the fog rows, which it then steps through again at the end anyway. The fog is now built in that last step alone. Same fog.
Shader values and bone matrices identical to what the GPU already has are not sent again.
Zombies no player can see update less often when your frame rate is high, as the game already does at lower frame rates.

On PCs with two graphics chips, which includes most gaming laptops, Windows often runs the game on the slower power-saving one built into the CPU. This sets the game to High performance in Windows' own graphics settings (Settings > Display > Graphics), so it runs on the dedicated GPU. A choice you already made there is kept, and turning this off removes the setting again. Does nothing on PCs with one graphics card.

Before drawing, the game asks the lighting engine about each square on screen, and a square whose light hadn't changed was asked again on every lookup, several times a frame. It's now asked once per lighting update. Same light.

Every launch and every save load the game compiles each Lua file it runs, its own and every mod's, from scratch. Compiled files are now kept in Zomboid/PZO/luacache.bin and reused while the file is unchanged, so starting the game and loading saves is quicker. The cache is rebuilt by itself after a game update.

Lua functions that run a lot (other mods', the game's and this one's) are turned into Java code after a few thousand instructions, so Java compiles them to machine code. In tests mod-style Lua ran 2 to 4 times faster. Function calls, errors and coroutines still go through the game's own Lua, so mods behave the same. A mod that misbehaves can be excluded below.

While new models load, the game raised an internal error for every bone it does not know (props, vehicle parts, modded rigs), and a model whose texture name the file system rejects failed and was logged again every time it loaded. Bones are now looked up in a table, and a bad texture name fails once and is logged once. Same result, fewer hitches while the world streams in.

Noises zombies can hear are listed in every chunk they reach. Those lists are now cleaned only in a frame where a noise actually ran out, instead of checking every loaded chunk every frame. Same noises.

The map of squares hidden behind upper floors was rebuilt almost every frame, because lights change a little all the time. It is now rebuilt only when walls, floors, cut-aways, the view or the zoom changed. Same picture. Single player only.
Answers queued path requests until the time below is used up, instead of the game's fixed 2 per pass, so zombies start moving sooner.
A faster priority queue inside the game's pathfinding library, so paths are found sooner in hordes and complex buildings.
Several changes to the same square in one pass are sent to the pathfinder as one.
A moving vehicle's shape is re-sent to the pathfinder only after it moves a quarter tile or every 250 ms.

Every few hundred sprites the game re-created, mapped and unmapped its sprite buffers, six driver calls each time and many times a frame at a wide zoom. With OpenGL 4.4 they now stay mapped and are written directly, so the CPU hands sprites to the graphics card with far less driver work. Same picture. Older graphics drivers keep the normal path.
Sets the 0.5 ms system timer, exempts the game from Windows power throttling, and on CPUs with enough cores uses MMCSS game scheduling and a higher process priority.

At medium and high puddle quality, every frame re-checked each puddle square on screen and worked out its corner lights and depths again. Squares, lights and depths are now kept per chunk and refreshed only when that chunk is redrawn, its lights change or the camera moves. Same picture.

At the lowest puddle quality, puddles are painted into each chunk's cached image, and while rain fills or dries them the game re-drew every loaded chunk, roofs and basements included, about once a second. Now only chunk floors that actually have puddles are re-drawn. Same picture.
Those once-a-second puddle re-draws are spread over about a quarter of a second instead of all landing in one frame. Until its turn, a chunk shows its puddles one tiny step (1/500) behind the rain.

While a world loads, the game checks the ID of every building and room on the map about six times. It only writes errors to the log and fixes nothing. The check is skipped unless the game runs in debug mode, so big and modded maps load faster.

A zombie that is not making any sound no longer recalculates its sound settings (floor material, distance, inside or out) every frame. They are worked out fresh the moment it makes a sound. Same sounds.

While the game starts and a save loads, finished textures wait in a queue for the graphics card. The game keeps that queue small and only sends it between loading-screen frames, so the loader threads often sit idle. The queue may now hold more (128 MB with 8 GB of RAM, 256 MB with 16 GB) and is sent as soon as work arrives. Nothing changes once you are playing.
The game profiler and the tile depth helper look up a per-thread value thousands of times a frame. On the game thread that value never changes, so it is now handed back straight away.

Chain-link fences, scaffolding, street decorations and ornamental plants near you are drawn into the chunk's cached image too, instead of one by one every frame. On a bench they were 91%% of what was still drawn every frame. They don't sway, so the picture is the same; ones the cache can't draw faithfully stay as they were.

Trees far from you are drawn into the chunk's cached image instead of one by one every frame, so they stop swaying in the wind. Trees near you, and large trees ahead of you while driving, are drawn as before.

Every update the game checked every crafting station, container and other object in the world to see if the player using it had walked away. Now only the objects someone is actually using are checked. Same result.
When the Java heap is about to need a collection, it is started in a frame that has time to spare, instead of landing mid-step during combat or driving.

When an area next to a horde loads, its zombies are created over a few frames instead of all in one long frame. Zombies within 25 tiles of you, and every zombie while you drive, still appear at once; none waits longer than half a second, and all are created before the game saves.

The distance zombies walk, crawl and run is added to the game's statistics once per frame instead of once per zombie, which also checks the achievements once instead of thousands of times. Same totals.
How many times a second dynamic lighting is recalculated. Auto leaves the game's own setting alone. Presets set this too.
Mods that force a full memory sweep mid-game are held back until you sleep, read or rest. Each repeated mod error is printed only 3 times. Broken vehicle repair recipes from mods are repaired.

Other mods' per-frame scripts run 60 times a second on average, spread over frames. At 60 FPS or less nothing changes, and they always run on a frame with a key or mouse press. Real Limbs and Project A-Life are left alone.

Other mods' scripts that run on every map square as it loads (LoadGridsquare) are queued and run over the next frames, about 2 ms per frame, squares nearest you first. With many mods this is most of the stutter while driving. A mod's change to a new square can show up a moment later. A mod that needs it straight away can be listed below.
Other mods' per-zombie scripts run every frame within 15 tiles of you, every 3rd frame to 30 tiles and every 6th beyond. Real Limbs and Project A-Life are left alone.
Runs the per-frame updates of Water Pipes and irrigation mods once a second. Only matters with those mods.
Moves dynamic lighting updates to a background thread. May cause short stalls in heavy combat.
Skips rebuilding the inventory item tooltip while the mouse is not moving.

Distance in tiles around the player to search for ground debris.

Removes discarded empty food cans, empty soda bottles, candy wrappers, and cigarette butts.
Removes naturally spawned foraging twigs, tree branches, and stones from roadways and paved areas (Logs and log stacks are permanently protected).
In-game hours between ground clutter and trash cleanup sweeps.
Optimizes cutaway wall and multi-story occlusion calculations for smooth interior frame rates.
Caps overlapping burning zombie scream sound loops.
Caps maximum active fire particles to 50 and vortices to 2 during large building and zombie fires.
Memory usage cutoff threshold required before Smart Idle Garbage Collection triggers a background sweep.
Runs gentle memory sweeps only when you are safely sleeping, reading, or resting indoors with zero nearby zombies.
Culls hidden lower floors and unviewable exterior ground tiles when inside multi-story buildings and skyscrapers. Automatically restores near windows & balconies.

Enables the mod's optimized screen-space puddle wave shaders and multi-pass wall shaders. Uncheck to bypass all custom shaders and use high-speed 2D flat tiles/puddles (recommended for Potato mode or if experiencing GPU driver glitches).
Disabling eliminates secondary reflection passes on roads and puddles, curing Build 42 driving and rain stutter.
Dynamically scales sub-pixel ground debris and skeleton blending when zoomed out to 150-250%% to eliminate zoom-out frame lag.
Forces texture compression in options.ini, cutting VRAM usage in half and stopping texture loading hitching.
Uncheck in Potato Mode to shade character/zombie meshes with ambient room light rather than per-vertex dynamic point lights.
Transitions distant zombies into stepped LOD animation poses sooner, eliminating frame drops when large swarms approach.
Limits simultaneous overlapping zombie groan and footstep audio emitters to the nearest 16 zombies to stop audio crackling and FMOD CPU lag.
[EXPERIMENTAL] Renders distant zombies in large 100+ hordes as 2D billboard imposters & enables GPU mesh instancing. WARNING: May cause micro-stutters during combat state transitions.
Skips skeletal mesh bone and animation math for zombies outside your camera view.
Staggers zombie A* navigation recalculations across a 4-phase round-robin cycle to drop swarm AI CPU load by 75%%.
Reduces skeletal animation update frequency for idle, sleeping, or standing characters to 15 FPS to save massive CPU cycles.
Hotkey used to toggle the Project Zomboid Optimiser Control Center (Default: F10)
Compiles character clothing, armor, and vehicle 3D textures across background CPU threads to eliminate equipment swap frame drops.
Directly patches IsoGridSquare.splatBlood in JVM bytecode to instantly return if a tile already has blood. Completely eliminates chunk FBO texture rebinding stalls in high-kill combats.
Number of world chunks retained in RAM cache for instant zero-lag road streaming.
Keeps recently streamed road and town chunks cached in 8GB+ RAM to completely eliminate disk read stutters when turning around or retracing paths.
Bypasses heavy wall-occlusion and low-pass DSP calculations for sounds beyond 35 tiles or below hearing threshold. Lowers audio thread CPU load during 100+ zombie combat.
Dynamically adjusts FSR render scale based on real-time frametime headroom against target FPS (down to 65%% or chosen scale) to absorb sudden horde or weather spikes.
Renders the 3D world at performance scale and reconstructs it with AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution (EASU + RCAS) while UI text stays native. Massive FPS boost on 1440p, 4K, and handhelds.
Upscaling render resolution preset. Ultra Quality (77%%) provides near-native image clarity with 30-50%%+ FPS gains; Performance (50%%) provides maximum boost.
Robust Contrast-Adaptive Sharpening strength (0%% = soft, 80%% = recommended, 100%% = max crispness).
Target memory threshold before gentle background GC sweeps cycle.
Filters redundant shader uniform uploads (lighting, fog, ambient color) and 3D clothing bone matrices before sending them to the GPU driver. Boosts FPS in dense cities.
Hibernates distant off-screen zombie pathfinding and animation state in RAM buffers to save massive CPU cycles in mega-horde territory.
Smoothly collects Lua garbage in 50-step increments every frame to prevent dead mod tables from accumulating and triggering 20-30ms stutter spikes during vehicle travel.
Answers queued path requests until a dedicated time budget is spent instead of vanilla strict 2-request cap, preventing pathing backlogs.
Replaces vanilla linear-scan decrease-key with indexed decrease-key in PZPathFind64.dll. Accelerates path search throughput during hordes and complex geometry.
Collapses repeated square updates within an iteration into the latest state, preventing redundant graph rebuilds and queue spam.
Resends vehicle navmesh polygons only when moving 0.25+ tiles or every 250ms, avoiding expensive DLL graph invalidation every micro-turn.
Locks Windows/Linux multimedia high-performance thread scheduling and prioritizes Performance Cores (P-Cores) over Efficiency Cores on Intel 12th-15th Gen and AMD X3D CPUs.
Immediately triggers a native JVM and Kahlua memory collection cycle to release unreferenced heap memory.
Enables 128KB page-aligned direct NIO memory stream buffers and ChunkBufferPool for stutter-free road chunk loading at 70+ mph.
Eliminates in-game stop-the-world Lua garbage collection pauses during combat and driving by offloading memory management to background G1GC worker threads.
Controls the target update framerate for dynamic lighting propagation. Lower values (15-30 FPS) save huge CPU cycles.

Inside a multi-story building, floors you cannot see are not drawn. Restored outside and in vehicles.
The game's wall, puddle and water shaders (on in vanilla). Turning them off saves GPU time but looks flatter. Turn off if you see shader glitches on your GPU.
The game's reflection pass on roads and puddles. Looks better, costs GPU, most of all in rain.
When zoomed out to 150 percent or more, fewer zombies get fully blended animations. Your normal setting comes back when you zoom in.
Turns on the game's texture compression in options.ini. Textures use far less video memory and load with fewer hitches.
Trees and bushes far from you are drawn into the chunk's cached image instead of being redrawn every frame with wind sway. Stands down when Atmospherics is active.
Lights characters and zombies with nearby light sources (on in vanilla). Off uses the room's ambient light instead.
Distant zombies switch to cheaper, stepped animation sooner.
Fewer zombies groan at once: only the nearest ones, as set below, get a voice (the game allows 20).
Items worn on belts, backs and holsters of zombies more than 25 tiles from you are not drawn. Their items are untouched and reappear as they come closer.
Distant zombies in large hordes are drawn as flat 2D images, with instanced rendering. May stutter when zombies change state.
Uses the game's animation delay for zombies outside your view, so their skeletons update less often.
Characters standing still, sleeping or idle update their animation 15 times a second instead of 30.
Clothing and vehicle textures larger than your texture size option are shrunk on a worker thread instead of in the frame, removing a 100 to 250 ms hitch per large texture.
A tile that already has blood gets no more, which avoids re-drawing its chunk image on every hit.
Lowers the render scale (down to 65 percent) when a frame runs over your target frame time, and raises it again when there is headroom.
Renders the world below your resolution and upscales it with FSR 1.0. The UI stays sharp.
Shader values and bone matrices identical to what the GPU already has are not sent again.
Zombies no player can see update less often when your frame rate is high, as the game already does at lower frame rates.
Answers queued path requests until the time below is used up, instead of the game's fixed 2 per pass, so zombies start moving sooner.
A faster priority queue inside the game's pathfinding library, so paths are found sooner in hordes and complex buildings.
Several changes to the same square in one pass are sent to the pathfinder as one.
A moving vehicle's shape is re-sent to the pathfinder only after it moves a quarter tile or every 250 ms.
Sets the 0.5 ms system timer, exempts the game from Windows power throttling, and on CPUs with enough cores uses MMCSS game scheduling and a higher process priority.
When the Java heap is about to need a collection, it is started in a frame that has time to spare, instead of landing mid-step during combat or driving.
How many times a second dynamic lighting is recalculated. Auto leaves the game's own setting alone. Presets set this too.
Mods that force a full memory sweep mid-game are held back until you sleep, read or rest. Each repeated mod error is printed only 3 times. Broken vehicle repair recipes from mods are repaired.

Other mods' per-frame scripts run 60 times a second on average, spread over frames. At 60 FPS or less nothing changes, and they always run on a frame with a key or mouse press. Real Limbs and Project A-Life are left alone.

Other mods' scripts that run on every map square as it loads (LoadGridsquare) are queued and run over the next frames, about 2 ms per frame, squares nearest you first. With many mods this is most of the stutter while driving. A mod's change to a new square can show up a moment later. A mod that needs it straight away can be listed below.
Other mods' per-zombie scripts run every frame within 15 tiles of you, every 3rd frame to 30 tiles and every 6th beyond. Real Limbs and Project A-Life are left alone.
Runs the per-frame updates of Water Pipes and irrigation mods once a second. Only matters with those mods.
